# Contributing

Thanks for taking an interest. This is a small project: an in-process add-on for CorelDRAW that
hosts an MCP server on loopback. Bug reports and documentation fixes are as welcome as code.

## What you need to build it

| Requirement | Why |
|---|---|
| Windows | the add-on is a `net48` assembly loaded into `CorelDRAW.exe` |
| .NET SDK able to build `net48` (verified with .NET 10) | `dotnet build` / `dotnet test` |
| A local CorelDRAW Graphics Suite 2025 (26) or 2026 (27) install | it is the only source of `Corel.Interop.VGCore.dll`, which every tool compiles against |
| WiX Toolset v5 | restored as a local dotnet tool (`dotnet tool restore`); needed only for the MSI |

There is **no way around the CorelDRAW install**: without `Corel.Interop.VGCore.dll` the project
does not compile. That is also why the build runs on a self-hosted Windows runner
(`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) — and why that workflow deliberately has **no `pull_request` trigger**:
a pull request from a fork would execute the fork's code on a machine that has CorelDRAW installed.
Pull requests are checked by `.github/workflows/docs.yml` instead, which is hosted and does not
need CorelDRAW. Do not merge the two files back together.

## Build, test, deploy

```powershell
dotnet build src\CorelMcpAddon\CorelMcpAddon.csproj -c Release -p:CorelDrawVersion=27
dotnet test  src\CorelMcpAddon.Tests\CorelMcpAddon.Tests.csproj -p:CorelDrawVersion=27

# elevated: build + copy into <CorelDRAW>\Programs64\Addons\CorelMcp
.\deploy\install.ps1
.\deploy\install.ps1 -Uninstall
```

CorelDRAW does not have to be running for the tests — they are plain xUnit tests over the tool
registry, the JSON layer, the JSON-RPC/HTTP layer, the config model, unit conversion and drawing
geometry. Close CorelDRAW before deploying: the running application holds the DLL open.

`-p:CorelDrawVersion=26` builds against CorelDRAW 2025 instead of 2026. The two releases ship
different interop assemblies, so a DLL built for one cannot be dropped into the other.

## Adding a tool

1. Add the registration in the matching `src/CorelMcpAddon/Tools/*.cs` file — a name, a
   description that explains the units and any surprise, a schema built with `Schema.*`, and the
   handler.
2. Give every parameter a description; a client's model sees only what you write there.
3. Cover it in `src/CorelMcpAddon.Tests/ToolCatalogTests.cs` (the registry is checked for
   uniqueness and schema sanity).
4. Describe it in `skills/coreldraw-mcp-drawing/references/tool-reference.md` — the skills are what
   a client's model reads. `docs/check-docs.ps1` fails when a registered tool is mentioned by no
   file under `skills/`.
5. Do not hard-code the tool count anywhere in prose — `tools/list` and `server_status` are the
   source of truth. `docs/check-docs.ps1` fails the build if a number sneaks back in.

## Documentation

- `README.md` and `README.ru.md` are kept in step: same headings, same order, same content.
  A change to one is a change to both.
- `docs/client-config.md` owns the `config.json` table and the tool group list.
- `docs/tools.md` owns the toolbox coverage checklist.
- `docs/installing.md` owns packaging and deployment.
- `skills/` owns the agent-facing instructions (setup, drawing, export). They are shipped, not
  local notes: changing a tool name, an argument or a default is a change to a skill too.
- Do not restate the same table in two files — link to the owner instead.

Run the checker before opening a PR:

```powershell
.\docs\check-docs.ps1
```

`check-docs.ps1` must stay **UTF-8 with BOM**: Windows PowerShell 5.1 reads a BOM-less script as
ANSI and mangles the Cyrillic patterns it matches against `README.ru.md`. Most editors keep the BOM
once it is there; do not "normalise" the file to BOM-less UTF-8.

## Installer assets

- `installer/Strings.en-US.wxl` and `Strings.ru-RU.wxl` must carry the **same Ids** with the same
  substitution fields. Adding a visible string means adding it to both.
- `installer/EULA.rtf` (English) and `EULA.ru.rtf` (Russian) are separate files on purpose: the
  licence in the dialog follows the package language.
- `installer/app.ico` is generated by `installer/make-icon.ps1` — edit the script and re-run it
  rather than replacing the binary by hand, so the icon stays reproducible.
- `installer/build-msi.ps1` builds one package per culture; `-Culture en-US` limits it to one.

## Pull requests

- Keep the diff focused; one topic per PR.
- No generated artefacts (`bin/`, `obj/`, `dist/`, `addon/`, `*.wixpdb`) in the commit.
- Do not bump `installer/version.txt` by hand — `installer/build-msi.ps1` does it on a
  successful build.
- Say how you verified the change: which tests ran, and whether you exercised it against a live
  CorelDRAW.
